newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end at record low for third day.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end at record low for third day.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended at a record closing low for the third successive day on Friday, after hitting an all-time low of 45.585 points, brokers said.
The index slipped 0.811 points or 1.74 percent to 45.676 points on volume of 4.4 million shares worth $1.6 million. Of 41 B shares, 37 traded with 17 down, 14 flat and six up.
Brokers said that recent continuous falls had hurt market sentiment and triggered more overseas institutional selling.
"Investors have lost confidence in the market with sluggish trading everyday," one broker said.
"According to the current rate of decline, we could see 42 points next week if there is no government policy support," a second broker said.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere was the biggest loser due to its plan to offer new B shares, plunging $0.050 or 11.36 percent to 0.390 on volume of 130,000 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power traded the most on heavy profit-taking after gains in the past few days, brokers said.
It ended down $0.014 or 3.48 percent to $0.388 on volume of 899,400 shares.
The market barometer, Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Devlopment, fell after its ex-rights today, which also hurt market sentiment, brokers said.
It closed down $0.019 or 2.28 percent to $0.812 on volume of 287,000 shares.
Shanghai A share index ends down in slow trading with investors remaining cautious, brokers said.

The A index dipped 8.736 points or 0.89 percent to 967.890 points on volume of 272.1 million shares worth 2.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index dropped 35.719 points or 1.47 percent to 2398.428 points.
Liyuan Hydraulic was the biggest loser on profit-taking, falling 0.75 yuan or 6.27 percent to 11.20 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
